messages:
julia_support: Hey @network — escalation from customer ACME (case 0123456789). Their service endpoint svc.internal.redwood.example.com is intermittently NXDOMAIN for pods in us-west-2, and sometimes resolves to the public IP (3.12.45.67). Bastion resolves to the private IP 10.0.5.12. E2E tests failing. Repro: from pod: `curl -v https://svc.internal.redwood.example.com` -> TLS cert CN=public.example.com and handshake fails. Can someone triage?

sam_net: Can you paste `dig +short` from both a pod and the bastion + the pod's /etc/resolv.conf? Also any node-local DNS (nodelocal) running?

julia_support: Pod dig output (from `kubectl exec -it test-pod -- dig +short svc.internal.redwood.example.com`):
```
3.12.45.67
```
Bastion dig (`dig +short svc.internal.redwood.example.com @10.0.5.2`):
```
10.0.5.12
```
Pod /etc/resolv.conf:
```
search default.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local
nameserver 169.254.169.253
options ndots:5
```
We do have a daemonset nodelocaldns running.

mike_infra: Interesting — pods are hitting a resolver that returns the public IP. Questions: 1) Do we have multiple Route53 private hosted zones with the same name? 2) Any Route53 Resolver rules forwarding that domain to a partner resolver? Run these: `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name internal.redwood.example.com` and `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules`/`list-resolver-rule-associations`.

julia_support: Pulled the AWS outputs: there are TWO private hosted zones for internal.redwood.example.com. One is associated to prod-vpc-123 (expected), the other to partner-vpc-999. Also there is a Route53 Resolver rule (rslvr-abcdef) forwarding internal.redwood.example.com to 10.0.2.100 and it's associated with prod-vpc-123.

eva_sre: That looks like a split-horizon + forwarding rule conflict. Even if a private hosted zone exists, an associated resolver rule can forward queries to a custom resolver for that domain. In this case queries from pods are getting forwarded to 10.0.2.100 (partner) which returns the public IP. Steps to confirm quickly:
- From a pod: `nslookup svc.internal.redwood.example.com 169.254.169.253`
- From node: `tcpdump -n -i any port 53 and host svc.internal.redwood.example.com` to see who we query.
- Check resolver rule associations: `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rule-associations --filters Name=ResolverRuleId,Values=rslvr-abcdef`
Also nodelocal can cache stale answers; after you fix rules you may need to restart the nodelocal daemonset to flush caches.

julia_support: Did a tcpdump on the node — saw queries sent to 10.0.2.100, not to the AmazonProvidedDNS IP. So the forwarder is being used. Customer wants minimal blast-radius fix.

mike_infra: Minimal fix = disassociate the resolver rule from prod-vpc-123 so queries hit the private hosted zone in prod-vpc-123. Command: `aws route53resolver disassociate-resolver-rule --resolver-rule-id rslvr-abcdef --vpc-id vpc-123` Then restart nodelocal: `kubectl rollout restart ds/nodelocaldns -n kube-system` (or delete pods) to clear cache. I'll schedule the change.

deploy-bot: Change scheduled 2026-03-17T22:10Z. Runbook:
1) Disassociate resolver rule `rslvr-abcdef` from `vpc-123`
2) Restart node-local DNS daemonset `kubectl rollout restart ds/nodelocaldns -n kube-system`
3) Verify: `kubectl exec -it test-pod -- dig +short svc.internal.redwood.example.com` should return `10.0.5.12`
4) Run customer e2e tests and check TLS: `curl -v https://svc.internal.redwood.example.com` cert CN should be `svc.internal.redwood.example.com` or matching SANs.

mike_infra: Performed step 1 and 2 during window. Verification: pod `dig +short` -> `10.0.5.12`. `curl -v` from pod now shows TLS handshake OK and peer cert CN matches private svc name. Customer ran e2e, all green. I'm going to follow up with partner to understand why their resolver rule got associated.

julia_support: Customer confirmed fix, tests passing. Will keep partner loop open. Adding reminder in runbook: check resolver-rule associations before onboarding partner VPCs. Case 0123456789 -> resolved. :white_check_mark: :tada:
